Hi Rachel,

We're updating our vendor registry for a new analysis pipeline and need to confirm a few items before we can authorize data flow to our EU analytics partner (NexaInsights). Specifically: 1) an up-to-date roster of all sub-processors who may access EU personal data for the relevant product (in particular any downstream analytics or logging partners); 2) a clear diagram or short description of encryption key custody (who holds keys, where are they stored, whether HSM/KMS is used, and if customer-managed keys are available); and 3) whether Redwood requires any amendment to our DPA to permit onwards processing to NexaInsights (we have SCCs in place but need explicit permission for this partner).

Would you be able to send the roster and a short key-flow diagram? We also attached our CAIQ-style checklist for the NexaInsights relationship — please confirm any gaps we should expect. We need this by Oct 8 to keep our scoping on track.

Thanks,
Vendor Security Team
EuroHealth Analytics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Thanks Rachel — quick technical summary below and I attached a diagram stub.

(a) In-scope vendors (short list):
- NexaInsights (prospective downstream analytics partner requested by EuroHealth) — would be a downstream processor we only engage after DPA amendment and limited-scoped onboarding.
- LogStream (log aggregation, EU region) — currently used for telemetry; processes pseudonymized telemetry for service health but not customer content by default; will appear on the roster.
- MetricsHub (aggregated usage metrics) — handles aggregated metrics; may receive tokenized identifiers.

(b) Key custody:
- Hosted (Redwood API): envelope encryption with Redwood-managed cloud KMS (provider-specific HSM-backed keys). Keys for customer workloads are isolated per-tenant in our KMS project but backing keys are Redwood-controlled by default.
- Dedicated/Private: customers may provide a key via BYOK (Google/AWS KMS or Customer HSM). In BYOK mode Redwood never stores the plaintext key; only wrapped key material is kept for handshake operations.
- NexaInsights flow: if EuroHealth requires NexaInsights to hold any derived keys or to perform decryption we require the customer to choose BYOK and a contractual amendment permitting the onward transfer. Without BYOK we can still route encrypted artifacts to NexaInsights but plaintext/shared-key access is not granted.

(c) DPA amendment: operationally we must add NexaInsights as an approved subprocessor and include a short clause that limits scope to the specific datasets and retention windows EuroHealth permits. We should also capture logging/audit access levels.

Attached: key_flow_diagram.pdf (draft). I can finalize after Neha confirms privacy language.

Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Ivan / EuroHealth team — thanks for the patience. Please find below and attached the packet you requested.

What I'm sending:
- vendor_roster_2026Q4.csv — current subprocessor roster with region and processing purpose (see attached CSV).
- key_flow_diagram.pdf — draft that shows Redwood-managed KMS flow vs BYOK flow (attached).
- dpa_amendment_draft.docx — redline we propose to add NexaInsights as an approved subprocessor and to document retention and audit access; this is conditional on EuroHealth signing the amendment.

Short answers to your bullets:
1) Roster: attached. LogStream and MetricsHub are already listed; NexaInsights will be listed only after we finalize the amendment and complete our onboarding checklist.
2) Encryption key custody: hosted customers - Redwood-managed KMS (Redwood has control of backing keys). Dedicated/Private - BYOK available (customer retains key material). If EuroHealth requires NexaInsights to decrypt data, we will only allow that path if EuroHealth elects BYOK and signs the DPA amendment; otherwise we will share only encrypted artifacts under the SCCs.
3) DPA amendment: attached draft. The amendment is narrow — it names NexaInsights, limits processing to the specific analytics pipeline, and requires audit logs and access controls.

Next steps: please review the attached DPA amendment and let us know if a countersignature is acceptable. If EuroHealth prefers BYOK, we can start a short onboarding thread for the key-handover procedure (expected ~2-3 weeks).

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the diagram.

Best,
Rachel Kim
